name: Evolent Health, Inc.

profile.description: Evolent Health, based in Arlington, Virginia, provides specialty care management for health plans, mainly in oncology and cardiology, through fee-based technology and services and risk-bearing 'Performance Suite' arrangements that aim to lower the total cost of care [4]. CEO Seth Blackley is building the company around AI-assisted prior authorization through its Auth Intelligence platform, which came from the 2024 Machinify deal [2]. Q2 2026 revenue was $652.5M (+46.9% YoY), and management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.6-2.7B with Adjusted EBITDA of $120-135M [1]. Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 5, 2026 [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Evolent has shifted from a broad value-based-care platform toward specialty care management and AI-enabled utilization management. It added Machinify's AI claims and authorization technology in 2024 (Machinify reviews over $200B in claims annually), and that capability now underpins Auth Intelligence [2]. AI Deployment (2/2): More than one-third of authorization volume that previously needed manual clinical review now runs through Auth Intelligence, and AI-approved cases complete in minutes instead of days; launches with Aetna and Highmark are showing early success [2]. Market Share (1/2): Evolent is a meaningful specialty-management vendor, and revenue grew 46.9% YoY in Q2 2026 on new contracts, but no category share data was found [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management has a stated long-term goal of auto-approving ~80% of authorization volume and named a new Chief Product Officer, but it gave no dated product launches [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports no separate R&D expense for FY2023-FY2025 [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Evolent's purpose is improving specialty care for patients with complex conditions while lowering the total cost of care, which is clear about what it does and for whom [4]. Its credibility suffers when the business is prior authorization for payers, and no evidence was found that the mission is distinctive among care-management vendors. Community Impact (0/2): No foundation or quantified community investment was found. Employee Retention (0/2): Management referenced 'a large RIF already announced', and the company described 'quickly changing staffing structures' as AI work accelerates, both negatives for retention [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP shows one open-market purchase (10,000 shares) in Q4 2025 and one insider sale in Q3 2026, roughly balanced over the last 12 months. An earlier cluster of 11 purchases in Q1 2025 falls outside the window [6].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth metrics. Revenue growth of 46.9% YoY scores 1.0, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 15.2% (FY2020 $925M to FY2025 $1.88B, derived from FMP statements) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [4][5]. The forward P/E of 11.0x scores 1.0 (yfinance) [4]. D/E of 253% scores 0.20. ROE of -67.0% (2x weight) and profit margin of -24.1% score 0.0, driven by a FY2025 net loss of $535M that came mostly from a ~$473M non-operating charge; operating loss was only $4M [5]. Forward PEG is excluded (null): the provider's forward PEG of -0.006 is computed off a negative earnings base and is not meaningful. Weighted sum 4.20 / 8 = 5.25, rounded to 5. Liquidity floor cleared at ~$11.0M average daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Evolent's core service, clinical review of specialty prior-authorization requests for health plans, is exactly the kind of rules-plus-judgment workflow AI is automating. Evolent is trying to be the automator: Auth Intelligence already handles more than a third of formerly manual review volume [2]. The exposure is real on two fronts. Payers could build or buy AI authorization tools directly and bypass outsourced vendors, and AI in coverage decisions faces political and regulatory scrutiny. Blackley has publicly said AI will never be used for adverse determinations [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Evolent reports AI adoption by volume but discloses no separate AI revenue figure, so the tiebreaker is not earned [2].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see a company that has reshaped itself repeatedly, often under outside pressure: activist Engaged Capital pushed it to exit True Health and explore a sale in 2020, it ran a sale process with private-equity interest in 2024, and in 2025-2026 it has cut staff while pivoting toward AI-driven authorization [2][3]. The stated purpose of better specialty care is service-oriented, but the strategic record reads more like a business optimizing for valuation and margins than one held together by a Just Cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Evolent's purpose of improving specialty care for complex patients while lowering cost has substance, but leadership communication focuses on revenue guidance, EBITDA ranges and membership assumptions (a 40% assumed decline in Performance Suite exchange membership) rather than a future patients would recognize [1][2]. The repeated willingness to sell the company suggests the cause does not anchor decisions [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Management cited a large reduction in force in 2025-2026, and the company described staffing structures as 'quickly changing' as AI automation scales, a classic setup for self-protection rather than psychological safety [2]. Repeated strategic reviews and activist involvement add further instability [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors' strengths or framing rivals as a source of learning; competitive messaging centers on Evolent's own contract wins and automation rates [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Evolent exited True Health after activist pressure, sharpened its focus on specialty care management, and is now rebuilding authorization around AI after the Machinify deal [2][3]. These are substantial changes, but they were driven by activist and financial pressure rather than by a Just Cause.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Investing in AI authorization, which cannibalizes manual clinical-review labor, is a costly long-term bet. So is Blackley's public commitment that AI will not make adverse determinations, a principled limit on automation [2]. However, the 2024 sale exploration and the cost-driven RIF point to near-term financial optimization [2][3].

investment_thesis: Evolent at $4.45 trades at ~0.24x sales and 11x forward earnings even though revenue is accelerating: Q2 2026 revenue of $652.5M grew 46.9% YoY and beat the $601.9M consensus, and FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $2.6-2.7B with Adjusted EBITDA of $120-135M [1][5]. Auth Intelligence gives Evolent a real AI cost lever. More than a third of formerly manual reviews now run through AI, AI approvals take minutes instead of days, and the long-term target is ~80% auto-approval, which could widen margins on fixed-fee contracts [2]. Q3 consensus revenue of ~$725-730M versus $480M a year ago points to continued strong growth [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance-sheet and business-model risk. FY2025 ended with a $535M net loss (ROE -67%, margin -24%), D/E is 253%, and tangible book value is negative (-$7.69/share) [4][5]. Risk-bearing Performance Suite contracts expose Evolent to cost-trend spikes in oncology and cardiology, and management already assumes a 40% decline in exchange membership in 2026 [2]. Prior authorization faces regulatory and political pressure, and payers could take AI authorization in-house. The company has a history of activist involvement and strategic reviews, plus a securities class action tied to the Passport Health Plan partnership [3]. For faith-aligned investors, the Inspire Impact Score of -67 (MISALIGNED, citing abortion and LGBT activism) is a major negative.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results on November 5, 2026 versus ~$725-730M revenue consensus and the raised $2.6-2.7B FY2026 revenue guide [1]
Auth Intelligence scaling toward the ~80% auto-approval goal, building on Aetna and Highmark launches and lowering clinical-review cost per case [2]
Deleveraging as Adjusted EBITDA of $120-135M and positive operating cash flow are directed at the 253% D/E balance sheet [1][5]
key_risks: Medical-cost risk in Performance Suite contracts — oncology drug and cardiology cost inflation can turn capitated contracts unprofitable, as the FY2025 $535M net loss showed [5]
Regulatory backlash against prior authorization and AI in coverage decisions could limit the automation thesis or force costly human-review requirements [2]
Leverage and negative tangible book value (-$7.69/share) leave little margin for error if contract losses or membership declines (40% assumed exchange drop) are worse than expected [2][5]
